content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) port of mk_depth.m for the FUNWAVE-TVD vessel_island_beach case: generates the depth grid and circling-vessel track file with a preview figure. Grid: 500x500 at dx=dy=2.0, centered coordinates (L10-L18). Bathymetry (L20-L41): base 10.0 (L25); r>R1=450 gives beach ring 10.0-(r-R1)*Slope (L32-L33); elif r<R2=100 gives island 10.0-(R2-r)*Slope_is (L35-L36), both slopes 0.24 (L22-L23); land capped at -2.0 via np.where (L40-L41). It plots -dep with terrain colormap and colorbar (L48-L55). Vessel track (L57-L89): Rs=R2-40.0, x0=Rs, y0=0.0, speed0=10.0 (L57-L60), t=range(0,301) (L74), radius ramps linearly to Rship=250 until t0=50 then stays (L76-L80), omega=speed0/Rship, angle=t*omega (L82-L83), appends xship/yship (L85-L86) and finite-difference speed ACTSP (L88-L89). Overlays the track (L92-L93), saves mk_depth.png (L96), then builds a 4-column vessel array (t, xship+m/2*dx, yship+n/2*dy, actsp) (L101-L105) and writes depth.txt and vessel_001.txt via np.savetxt (L107-L108).
entities: script (no function/class definitions; top-level Python script)
j, i — grid loop indices (L27, L28)
xship, yship — vessel track lists (L62-L66, L85-L86)

unresolved: Differences from the MATLAB sibling: the vessel file here has 4 columns including actsp (L101-L105) and is named vessel_001.txt, versus 3 columns and vessel_0001 in mk_depth.m; which format the FUNWAVE-TVD vessel module actually expects is not determinable from this file.
plt.hold(True) (L92) was removed in matplotlib 3.0, so the script fails on modern matplotlib.
The elif at L35 makes beach and island branches exclusive (identical net behavior to the MATLAB two-if version because r cannot be both >450 and <100, but structurally different).
Same spin-up inconsistency as the MATLAB version: angle uses omega=speed0/Rship while rship<Rship during t<t0, so actual speed is below speed0 (L76-L88).
np.savetxt default format writes full-precision scientific notation; whether FUNWAVE-TVD readers accept this for depth.txt/vessel_001.txt is not verifiable here.
